Reflecting On Diversified Banks Stocks' Q3 Earnings: Bank of America (NYSE:BAC)

Quarterly earnings results are a good time to check in on a company's progress, especially compared to its peers in the same sector. Today we are looking at Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) and the best and worst performers in the diversified banks industry.

At their core, diversified banks take in deposits and engage in various forms of lending, which means revenue is generated through interest rate spreads (difference between loan and deposit rates) and fees. Other revenue comes from adjacent services such as wealth management, card and account fees, and products such as annuities. These institutions benefit from rising interest rates that improve NIMs (net interest margins), digital transformation reducing operational costs, and expanding wealth management services as populations age. However, they face headwinds including fintech competition disrupting traditional models (how disruptive is crypto?), stringent regulatory requirements increasing compliance costs, and cybersecurity threats requiring substantial technology investments. Economic downturns also pose risks through potential loan defaults and compressed margins during accommodative monetary policy periods.

The 7 diversified banks stocks we track reported a slower Q3. As a group, revenues missed analysts' consensus estimates by 0.7%.

While some diversified banks stocks have fared somewhat better than others, they have collectively declined. On average, share prices are down 1.8% since the latest earnings results.

Bank of America (NYSE:BAC)

Tracing its roots back to 1784 and now serving approximately 67 million consumer and small business clients, Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) is a global financial institution that provides banking, investing, asset management, and risk management products and services to individuals, businesses, and governments.

Bank of America reported revenues of $30.1 billion, up 3.1% year on year. This print fell short of analysts' expectations by 1.5%. Overall, it was a softer quarter for the company with a significant miss of analysts' EPS estimates and a slight miss of analysts' tangible book value per share estimates.

Bank of America Total Revenue

The market seems disappointed with the results as the stock is down 6.6% since reporting and currently trades at $50.41.

title: JPMorgan (JPM): Can New Branches Keep Winning Profitable Customers?
detail:
JPMorgan (JPM): Can New Branches Keep Winning Profitable Customers?
Jeff Lewis

JPM
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) is expanding branches while competitors invest in their own networks. Physical access can bring in deposits, investment accounts, and business borrowers. The financial test is retaining deposits without overpaying for them, then earning enough across each relationship to cover acquisition and servicing costs.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) trades at 13x forward P/E versus 14x trailing P/E. Trailing P/E uses the past 12 months' earnings; forward P/E uses forecast earnings. Exceptional gains can lower a historical multiple without improving recurring profit. Q2 reported EPS was $7.70, or $6.14 excluding significant securities gains. Continued deposit and fee growth must support the earnings outlook.

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) trades at 10x forward P/E. Analysts expect roughly 4% adjusted EPS growth in 2027 versus 2026 for JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM), compared with 14% for the peer. Both groups also earn wealth and investment-banking fees, so their multiples value broader businesses. The premium therefore needs support from earnings durability. The valuation is fair given the established franchise's profitability, with branch expansion offering further growth.

Read more: 12 Most Profitable Cheap Stocks to Buy Right Now

JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM): It's The Best Of The Bunch Right Now, Says Jim Cramer
A Branch Can Win More Than a Deposit Account

JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM), included in Insider Monkey's list of undervalued financial stocks, attributes approximately 40% of deposit-share gains since 2019 to new branches. Yet national retail deposit share slipped to 11.1% in 2025. Expansion has contributed meaningfully without guaranteeing annual share gains. Management says 80% of consumer clients consider it their primary bank. Payroll and bill-payment habits can make such accounts harder to switch, reducing reliance on promotional rates.

The attraction is selling additional services without repeatedly paying to find new customers. JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) says 90% of first-time wealth investors came through branch referrals in 2025. Only 21% of its more than five million affluent banking households invested with it, leaving room to deepen existing relationships.

Advisory fees can supplement lending income, but investment assets must translate into durable fee earnings. Market appreciation can lift balances without stronger customer acquisition. Advisor compensation and service costs also absorb part of the revenue.

For JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM), small-business relationships offer deposits, payments, and credit revenue. However, average Business Banking loans fell 5% in Q2 2026. Turning customer knowledge into sound lending requires credit discipline: loan growth creates value only after funding costs, losses and capital requirements.

title: Bank of America (BAC): Is Its Deposit Franchise Getting Stronger as Lending Accelerates?
detail:
Bank of America (BAC): Is Its Deposit Franchise Getting Stronger as Lending Accelerates?
Jeff Lewis
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 6:38 AM MST 4 min read
BAC
WFC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) is growing lending faster than deposits, but the more useful question is what that funding costs. Second-quarter average loans increased 8% year over year while deposits rose 2%. Consumer balances grew approximately 1%, against 8% in Global Banking. Nevertheless, net interest income increased 9%, showing that uneven deposit growth can coexist with improving lending economics.

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) trades at approximately 11x forward P/E versus 13x trailing P/E. Higher lending and fee income, operating leverage, and share repurchases support the earnings improvement behind that gap. The forward valuation sits above Wells Fargo & Company (NYSE:WFC) at 10x and below JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) at 14x. It looks reasonable if inexpensive deposits sustain earnings growth after credit costs.

Also read: 10 Most Active Blue Chip Stocks to Buy Right Now

Dividend Growth in the Banking Sector: Bank of America (BAC)'s Path to Consistent Dividends
Checking Relationships Still Lower Funding Costs

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) increased average Consumer Banking deposits to $957 billion from $950.8 billion in the first quarter, extending the recovery from $945 billion in late 2025. The rate paid on those deposits fell to 0.48%, from 0.58% a year earlier. Growing balances while paying less interest gives the lending business a practical advantage over financing that must continually compete on yield.

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) estimates that 92% of consumer checking accounts are customers' primary accounts. Direct deposits, payments and everyday banking create reasons to stay beyond the advertised interest rate. Those relationships become an earnings advantage when customer loyalty supports profitable lending, provided technology, service and credit costs remain controlled.

For Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC), interest-rate changes affect both sides of the spread. Lower deposit rates reduce funding expense, while repricing older fixed-rate assets can raise income. Loan growth and market activity also contributed to net interest income of $16 billion. Tax-equivalent net interest yield, a non-GAAP measure adjusting for tax-exempt interest, increased to 2.08% from 1.94% a year earlier. The lesson from cheaper funding and better lending returns is that savings matter alongside asset yields and credit performance.

Faster Lending Must Preserve Returns

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) paid 2.23% on Global Banking deposits, substantially more than on consumer balances. Corporate deposits can support lasting payments and cash-management relationships, but faster growth in this category can increase the funding mix's sensitivity to rates. Sustained consumer deposit growth would strengthen the franchise by limiting the need to attract more expensive incremental balances.

title: Bank of America vs. Goldman Sachs: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

Bank of America vs. Goldman Sachs: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Erin Kennedy, The Motley Fool

BAC
GS
FMCC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Choosing between a retail banking powerhouse and a Wall Street institutional leader requires balancing stability against market-driven growth. Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) and Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS) offer distinct ways to play the financial sector.

Bank of America serves as a cornerstone of the American economy through its vast branch network and consumer lending operations. Goldman Sachs remains the premier name in investment banking and global markets, though it is currently refining its strategy by narrowing its focus on core institutional and wealth clients.

The case for Bank of America

Bank of America operates a massive, diversified financial services business that reaches nearly every corner of the credit market. It remains a dominant force among bank stocks due to its scale, serving roughly 70 million consumers and small businesses through thousands of financial centers. The company also maintains critical relationships with government-sponsored enterprises, including Freddie Mac, for residential mortgage sales and servicing.

Financial performance remains steady despite shifting interest rate environments. In fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $191.6 billion, representing a slight year-over-year decline of approximately 0.5%. The company generated net income of nearly $30.5 billion during this period, achieving a net margin of nearly 15.9%, representing the percentage of revenue retained as profit after all expenses.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 1.2. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to show how much a company relies on borrowed money. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations using short-term assets, was approximately 0.4. Free cash flow reached nearly $12.6 billion, and note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 31.7% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation because it is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Goldman Sachs

Goldman Sachs is a global leader in high finance, focusing on investment banking, market-making, and asset management. In its latest annual report, filed for the period ending December 2025, the firm highlighted its One Goldman Sachs initiative designed to integrate services for corporate and institutional clients. The company is currently in a transition period as it exits consumer credit partnerships, such as the credit card program with Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), to return to its core strengths.

title: KEY Q3 Earnings Beat as NII, Fee Income Increases Y/Y & Provisions Dip
detail:
KEY Q3 Earnings Beat as NII, Fee Income Increases Y/Y & Provisions Dip
Zacks Equity Research
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 4:32 AM MST 5 min read
KEY
BAC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

KeyCorp's KEY third-quarter 2026 earnings from continuing operations of 51 cents per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 46 cents. The bottom line reflected a 24.4% rise from the prior-year quarter.

Results primarily benefited from higher net interest income (NII) and non-interest income. Higher average loan balances, along with lower provisions, were other tailwinds. However, higher expenses hurt the results to some extent.

Net income from continuing operations attributable to common shareholders was $537 million, up from $454 million in the prior-year quarter.

KEY's Revenues Improve, Expenses Rise

Total revenues (taxable-equivalent or TE) increased 8.3% year over year to a record $2.05 billion. The top line surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.03 billion.

NII (TE basis) jumped 9.6% from the prior-year quarter to $1.31 billion. The net interest margin (TE basis) from continuing operations expanded 20 basis points (bps) to 2.95%. Both metrics benefited from lower deposit costs as a result of declining interest rates and proactive deposit beta management, the reinvestment of proceeds from maturing low-yielding investment securities and fixed-rate swaps into higher-yielding investments, an expanding balance sheet and a continued strategic shift toward higher-yielding commercial and industrial loans. These benefits were partially offset by the impact of lower interest rates on repricing earning assets.

Non-interest income was $744 million, up 6% year over year. The rise was mainly driven by higher investment banking and debt placement fees, trust and investment services income, and cards and payments income. These were partially offset by lower commercial mortgage servicing fees.

Non-interest expenses increased 5.8% year over year to $1.25 billion. The rise was predominantly due to an increase in personnel expenses, primarily related to continued investments in people, employee benefits and incentive compensation associated with non-interest income growth. These were partially offset by a decline in other expenses.

At the end of the third quarter, average total loans were $111.59 billion, up 1.4% from the previous quarter and 5% year over year. Average total deposits were $151.18 billion, up 2.4% sequentially and 0.5% year over year.

KEY's Credit Quality Improves

The provision for credit losses was $61 million, down 43% from the prior-year quarter.

Net loan charge-offs, as a percentage of average total loans, declined 10 bps year over year to 0.32%. Also, non-performing assets, as a percentage of period-end portfolio loans, other real estate-owned property assets and other non-performing assets, were 0.55%, down 8 bps.

The allowance for loan and lease losses was $1.40 billion, down 3.2% year over year.

Is BE Semiconductor Industries Fairly Priced on Cash Flow?
